build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 8: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 10's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 4-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 8's value table (side 1's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 8's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0043, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0027 and 0 for channels 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 8 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 7, frame 2 then 1, frame 3 then 1, frame 4 then 1, frame 5 then 1, frame 6 then 1, frame 7 then 1, frame 8 then 30. One pass takes 43 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 9 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 9 then 1, frame 10 then 1, frame 11 then 1, frame 11 then 1, frame 10 then 3, frame 12 then 5, frame 11 then 5, frame 11 then 1, frame 12 then 6. One pass takes 24 steps.

Picture 8's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 31 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 1: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 3 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 6 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 9 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 11 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 22 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 8 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 22 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 16 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 32 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 12 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 17 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 6 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
Frame 9 of picture 8, named by channel 1's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 10 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 1 block of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 4 bitmap bytes in all, in column 4. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 11 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 3, 4, 7 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 7 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 4. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 12 of picture 8, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 6 and 9: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 7 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 4. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

The last byte picture 8's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,092nd byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. It is the same on every side that holds the picture, and nothing reads it.
